title: Election
definition: Election is God's gracious choice in Christ to save a people for Himself before the foundation of the world.
summary: Election teaches that salvation rests on God's gracious purpose in Christ, not on foreseen merit or human boasting.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the chosen and beloved Son in whom God's people are chosen, redeemed, and brought safely home.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Election directs attention to God's eternal grace before it looks at the believer's response in time. The doctrine does not make Christ unnecessary; it shows that God's saving purpose is fulfilled in Christ and applied by the Spirit. It humbles the redeemed, strengthens worship, and reminds the Church that salvation begins in mercy rather than human deserving.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because pride quickly tries to take credit for what grace alone has done. Election protects assurance by grounding salvation in God's purpose, not in the instability of human strength. It also fuels mission because God has people whom He will call through the Gospel.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let election produce humility, worship, courage, and evangelistic prayer. Do not use it as an excuse for coldness or speculation. Rest in God's mercy, proclaim Christ freely, and treat every sinner as someone who must hear the Gospel.
